dispute_ticket.description: My passenger spilled curry all over the back seat and just walked off. I had to pay $150 for cleaning. I am attaching the photos and I want the cleaning fee charged to the rider.

dispute_history.note: includes a cleaning claim rejected 2026-08-14 for photos that predated the trip

chat_logs.content: I'm at the City Square pickup point, blue Shuttle.
Hi, I saw a cleaning charge notification? We didn't have any food with us, we came from the cinema.

app_events.details: Rider R-8140 booked trip RYDE-DEMO-021 from City Square Mall to Serangoon North.
Driver submitted cleaning claim S$150.00 with 2 photos of a curry spill on the rear seat. Photo metadata timestamps: 2026-09-28 17:21 and 17:23 (3 hours BEFORE this trip's pickup at 20:32).
Driver submitted a handwritten receipt for S$150.00 with no shop name or registration number.

platform_policy.cleaning_claim_evidence_required: photos taken promptly after the trip and a receipt where available
platform_policy.rider_may_dispute_if: evidence does not show the mess, predates the trip, or the fee exceeds the actual cleaning cost

expected_outcome.reason: The claim's own evidence contradicts it: both photos were taken at 17:21-17:23, three hours before this trip's 20:32 pickup, so they cannot show a mess made on this trip, and the receipt is handwritten with no shop identity. The driver also had a cleaning claim rejected in August for the same photos-predate-trip pattern. Hard in-case evidence of a fake claim plus a repeat pattern is exactly what routes to a person: a human reviewer should deny the claim and decide whether to confirm a fraud flag against the driver, which the system must not do on its own.
expected_outcome.fraud_note: FRAUD EVAL F2 (fake claim, hard evidence): photo EXIF predates the trip + similar rejected claim in history. Expected risk HIGH -> human review with full report. The system must not auto-charge the rider and must not auto-flag the driver as a fraudster.
